name: Coke La Rock
hook: Talked over Kool Herc's records at the first party and is widely called the first MC, having released nothing and been credited for less.

blurb.age7: At the very first hip-hop party, he was the one talking on the microphone between the records.
blurb.age13: Coke La Rock was Kool Herc's friend and got on the microphone at Herc's parties from 1973. At first he did not even have a stage name and stood out of sight, so the crowd had no idea who was talking. What he said was mostly shout-outs to people he knew in the room, which is where rapping starts: not as poetry, but as one person naming his friends over a record. Phrases he used turned up later on 'Rapper's Delight', the first rap hit, with no credit to him.
blurb.adult: The clearest example on this map of foundational work that produced no property. La Rock's contribution predates the recording industry's involvement in hip-hop, was improvised in rooms nobody was taping for release, and entered the commercial record through phrases other people sold. He is here for what he started, and the absence of a discography is the historically interesting fact about him rather than a gap in the data.
